sources.title: Reinhold Kaiser, Historical Dictionary of Switzerland: Burgondes
sources.note: Rhine kingdom, 436 destruction, 443 settlement, Rhône expansion, 532 defeat and 534 Frankish partition; archaeological identity and integration.

sources.title: Université Grenoble Alpes: Lex Romana Burgundionum
sources.note: Primary Latin edition: titles 11.5, 29, 35.1, 36.1 and heading 36. Page dating differs from modern Cologne scholarship; use early sixth century.

sources.title: Universität zu Köln, Bibliotheca legum: Lex Romana Burgundionum
sources.note: Compilation probably later 510s under Gundobad or Sigismund; Roman sources; one nearly complete manuscript, Vat. Lat. 7277, plus fragments.

sources.title: Historical Dictionary of Switzerland: Saint-Maurice, abbaye
sources.note: 515 foundation by Sigismund and laus perennis, successive singing choirs; avoid disputed endpoint of practice.

sources.title: Abbaye de Saint-Maurice: Agaune and the Burgundian kingdom
sources.note: 515 foundation ceremony, Avitus sermon and Rhône/Alpine-route setting.

sources.title: Canton de Genève: Archéologie genevoise 2021 to 2022
sources.note: Printed page 79: Aire-la-Ville cemetery and comparison with Sézegnin, over 700 graves, late fourth to eighth centuries; burial structures change.

sources.title: Canton de Genève: Archéologie genevoise, report on Saint-Antoine
sources.note: Printed page 29: burial ages, missing youngest children possibly buried separately; material/cultural identification must remain cautious.

sources.title: Treccani, Enciclopedia dell’Arte Medievale: Sicilia, Epoca islamica
sources.note: 827 conquest begins, Aghlabid/Fatimid/Kalbid phases; Palermo 1072 and Noto 1091. Kalbid accession varies 947/948 between sources; use mid-tenth century.

sources.title: Lundy and colleagues, PLOS ONE: New insights into early medieval Islamic cuisine
sources.note: 2021 study, 134 cooking pots, ninth to twelfth centuries, Palermo and Casale San Pietro; lipid residues, rural dairy, no fish biomarkers, limits of inference.

sources.title: University of York: Thriving wine trade in medieval Islamic Sicily
sources.note: Chemical evidence from ninth to eleventh-century amphorae in Sicily, Sardinia and Pisa; probable wine trade does not establish religion of drinkers.

sources.title: University College London: Ceramics for economic history, Islamic Palermo
sources.note: Viva Sacco’s research monograph: late ninth to eleventh-century pottery production, circulation and chronology.

sources.title: University of York: Sicily in Transition
sources.note: Castronovo landscape, Monte Kassar, citadel and Casale San Pietro; centuries of changing settlement, not one frozen Islamic village.

sources.title: British Museum: quarter-dinar, 1877,0406.14
sources.note: Al-Zahir quarter-dinar minted Sicily 1029/AH420; gold, 14mm, 0.96g, Arabic legends.

sources.title: Ibn Hamdis, Qadat fi al-siba al-nafs awtaraha, primary poem transcription
sources.note: Primary text directly read; exact quoted hemistich: فإن كنتُ أخرجت من جنةٍ. Later exile poem, not an emirate-era inscription; poet recalls age sixty. Cross-checked against University of Diyala paper, printed page8, citing Diwan page183.

sources.title: Ziyad Tariq Lafta al-Ubaydi, University of Diyala: Ibn Hamdis al-Siqilli, thematic and artistic study
sources.note: Literary study: introduction and biography on displacement; printed page8 reproduces paradise verse and cites Diwan page183. PDF text extraction has damaged letters/numerals; verse also directly checked in Wikisource transcription.

sources.title: Christopher Storrs: La politica internazionale, in I Savoia
sources.note: University of Turin repository; 1559 restoration, Sardinian crown 1720, Restoration and transformation into Italy 1861.

sources.title: MuseoTorino: Storia di Torino, Capitale dello Stato assoluto
sources.note: Chapter V: French occupation 1536, capital transferred from Chambéry 1563; page 136 silk hand labor and mechanization.

sources.title: MuseoTorino: L’economia della seta nel Seicento
sources.note: Municipal water-powered silk mill initiative 1665; Galleani’s Venaria works 1670 with training school and visible machinery.

sources.title: MuseoTorino: I Molassi, ex mulini della città
sources.note: Municipal grain mills on Dora, medieval origins, increased capacity in 1679.

sources.title: MuseoTorino: Court and civic ceremonies, 1563 entry
sources.note: Part 2: Marguerite’s formal entry on 7 February 1563, canopy and municipal preparations and expenses.

sources.title: Regione Autonoma della Sardegna: Historical guide
sources.note: Italian replaces Spanish in official/school use 1760; Cagliari reopened 1764, Sassari 1765; enclosures 1820 and administrative fusion 1847.

sources.title: SardegnaForeste: Editto delle chiudende 1820
sources.note: Regional forest agency, discussion by Enea Beccu: intended property reform and disputes over communal land access.

sources.title: MuseoTorino: Piccola casa della Divina Provvidenza
sources.note: 27 April 1832 Valdocco start in stable/hayloft/room; poor sick people excluded elsewhere; legal recognition 1833 and hospital opening 1834.

sources.title: MuseoTorino: Primo tratto di acquedotto
sources.note: Poor well/fountain water; construction 1853 to 1859; Val Sangone supply and 6 March 1859 fountain inauguration.

sources.title: Statuto Albertino, 4 March 1848, primary Italian text
sources.note: Article 24 equality formula quoted exactly; articles 1, 2 and 33 distinguish state religion, monarchy, royal-appointed Senate.

sources.title: MuseoTorino: Lo Statuto Albertino
sources.note: 4 March 1848 royal grant after demonstrations and constitutional movement.

sources.title: Haus der Bayerischen Geschichte: Königreich Bayern
sources.note: Kingdom 1 January 1806 to November1918; territorial integration and secularization. Avoid oversimplification of Jewish equality in overview.

sources.title: Haus der Bayerischen Geschichte: School regulation 23 December 1802
sources.note: School attendance ages6 to 12, fees paid by parents, leaving examination, Sunday school12 to 18.

sources.title: Bavarian State Archives: Impfgegner, archival exhibition
sources.note: Mandatory smallpox vaccination in 1807; Regierungsblatt 1807, columns 1426 to 1437, reproducing columns 1427 to 1428.

sources.title: Haus der Bayerischen Geschichte: Bayerisches Judenedikt, 1813
sources.note: Primary edict of 10 June 1813: school access in section 32; household registration and settlement restrictions in sections 12 to 13.

sources.title: German Patent and Trade Mark Office: Alois Senefelder
sources.note: Munich lithography in 1796: playwright’s printing costs, limestone and grease/water behavior; music publisher André in 1799.

sources.title: Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft: Joseph von Fraunhofer
sources.note: Solar spectrum measurements in 1814; earlier observation by Wollaston in 1802; optical calibration, with chemical interpretation coming later.

sources.title: DB Museum: The Adler
sources.note: Nuremberg to Fürth railway, 1835: Stephenson manufacture, transport taking over two months, assembly and driver William Wilson; present engines are replicas.

sources.title: City of Munich official Oktoberfest: History
sources.note: Wedding and horse race in October 1810; children’s presentations; agricultural festival in 1811, municipal organization in 1819. Ludwig was crown prince, not Prince Regent as the page says.

sources.title: Universität Würzburg: Constitution of Bavaria, 26 May 1818
sources.note: Preamble exact Freyheit der Meinungen, mit gesetzlichen Beschränkungen gegen den Mißbrauch. Historical spelling retained.

sources.title: Bavarian State Archives: Revolution in Weißenburg, 1848
sources.note: Printed page 10: annual cartload of forest leaves granted in Weißenburg in 1848, used for bedding for small livestock; surplus sold for city funds.

sources.title: Free State of Saxony: Königreich Sachsen
sources.note: Kingdom from 1806, territorial partition in 1815, constitutional change and 1848 to 1849 revolution; monarchy ended in 1918.

sources.title: Saxon Ministry of Justice: The first constitution
sources.note: Protests in 1830 and constitution in 1831; Anton and Friedrich August; legal challenge to administrative action under section 49.

sources.title: Technische Universität Chemnitz: Institutional history
sources.note: Royal Technical School founded in 1836 in response to demand for technical training.

sources.title: Technische Universität Chemnitz: Library history
sources.note: Early school library, 1836 to 1862: machinery, chemistry, textiles, geography, roads, surveying and economics.

sources.title: Industriemuseum Chemnitz: Museumskurier 25, 2010
sources.note: Article by Künzel and Lang: Carl Julius Borcherdt’s workshop began in 1835 and engine was completed in 1836, based on contemporary accounts from 1843 to 1844; rejects unsupported 1829 date.

sources.title: Förderverein Göltzschtalbrücke: Bridge history
sources.note: Construction in 1846 to 1851; weak ground prompted redesigned central arches; average workforce about 770.

sources.title: Förderverein Göltzschtalbrücke: Stefan Näherlich, railway viaduct
sources.note: About 26 million bricks, local clay and granite at points of high stress; opening on 15 July 1851.

sources.title: Technische Universität Dresden: Midwifery history
sources.note: Indexed institutional history: Carus directed the royal midwives’ school from 1814 and taught obstetrics until 1827.

sources.title: Hochschule für Musik und Theater Leipzig: History
sources.note: Mendelssohn’s conservatory opened on 2 April 1843.

sources.title: Robert Schumann: Musikalische Haus- und Lebensregeln, 1850
sources.note: Primary first printing: Neue Zeitschrift für Musik, volume 32, supplement to number 36, 3 May 1850, pages 1 to 4. Rule 10: Spiele immer, als hörte dir ein Meister zu. Also ear training, finger exercises and rest.

sources.title: Landesarchiv Baden-Württemberg: Kingdom of Württemberg, 1806 to 1918
sources.note: State archive project on historical statistics for the Kingdom of Württemberg, 1806 to 1918.

sources.title: Landesarchiv Baden-Württemberg: Estates and constitution
sources.note: Chapter 6: abolition of old constitution in 1805; negotiated constitution in 1819; Uhland; rump parliament in 1849; federal context from 1871.

sources.title: Universität Würzburg: Constitution of Württemberg, 25 September 1819
sources.note: Primary constitution, section 6: seat of government cannot move outside the kingdom; section 4: powerful king under the constitution.

sources.title: Universität Hohenheim: History, 1800 to 1932
sources.note: Famine in 1816 following Tambora; agricultural teaching, experimental and model institute in 1818. Schwerz, two other teachers, 16 pupils, six subjects, affiliated farm and orphanage.

sources.title: State Palaces and Gardens Baden-Württemberg: Queen Katharina’s initiatives
sources.note: Charity association in 1817; higher school for girls, savings bank and Cannstatt festival in 1818. Elite education is not universal schooling.

sources.title: Stadtarchiv Stuttgart: Katharinenhospital
sources.note: Municipal archive study published in 2022: built in 1820 to 1827 and opened in 1828, addressing obsolete and undersized facilities.

sources.title: City of Stuttgart: Bad Cannstatt
sources.note: First railway from Cannstatt to Untertürkheim in 1845; mineral water resort and affluent eighteenth- and nineteenth-century visitors.

sources.title: Baden-Württemberg education server: Railway history
sources.note: Rosenstein tunnel constructed in 1844 to 1846 beneath the palace axis and a 200-meter Neckar bridge. Stuttgart connection followed the first Cannstatt train.

proposedOverrides.summary: Kingdom of Sardinia across mainland and island phases, transformed into the Kingdom of Italy in 1861.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Checked the Rhine geometry in 400 and Rhône/Sapaudia geometry in 500. This is the early medieval kingdom, not the later duchy. Political conquest in 534; imported map coverage ends in 600.

Checked island geometry in 900 and 1000. The label covers Aghlabid, Fatimid, Kalbid and fragmented governments. Norman conquest completed in 1091, before map endpoint 1100. Ibn Hamdis poem is explicitly a later exile witness.

Mainland geometry in 1530, 1600, 1650 and 1700 continues the Savoyard state. The Sardinian name is premature in 1650; crown acquired in 1720. Map shows mainland in 1783, island only in 1800, and both in 1815. Shared narrative explains changing constituent territories, not unchanged borders. Transformation into Italy in 1861, not 1878.
Electorate in 1783, kingdom from 1806; monarchy ended in 1918. The second polygon in 1783 has an implausibly large bounding box. Geometry checked for identity only and not certified as accurate.
Both records begin in 1783, before kingdom status in 1806. Saxon geometry in 1815 reflects territorial loss. Imported map coverage ends in 1878; monarchies ended in 1918.
